hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: A daemon-owned, self-describing settings contract feeds a native JetBrains Settings page that renders whatever the daemon reports. The plugin adds config gateway methods behind the established sealed three-state result pattern and a native applicationConfigurable built purely from the daemon's description. Reads use the catalog IPC plus the existing value read; writes reuse the existing segment-aware write. The plugin owns no settings semantics; the daemon stays the single source of truth.

consumedContracts.name: Self-describing settings catalog (enriched ConfigOption + role taxonomy) over config.catalog, and its plugin read surface
consumedContracts.purpose: The single daemon-owned description the whole IDE surface renders from: settings + the recognized roles/tiers + current values.

consumedContracts.name: Settings write surface (segment-aware write + clear) behind a sealed SaveResult
consumedContracts.purpose: The one way the IDE persists an edit: a segment-array write + a clear that removes a key, each returning a sealed SaveResult. Reused by both override editors.

consumedContracts.name: Settings page framework (Configurable host + grouped collapsible rendering + type→control mapping)
consumedContracts.purpose: The native applicationConfigurable + rendering scaffold, exposing the SettingsSection extension point where the dynamic-key sub-sections plug in.

boundary.internal: Wholly private to s4: the per-role overrides sub-section — listing roles from sc1, showing override vs default routing, and add/change/remove that writes or clears models.tasks.<roleId> via sc2. Plugs into sc3's SettingsSection seam; introduces no contract others consume.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Daemon-side catalog enrichment + config.catalog assembly stay private to s1; other stories consume only the sc1 payload shape.
Read-only rendering + collapsible layout + the daemon-unavailable placeholder stay private to s2; the SettingsSection seam is declared here.
Per-type edit controls + validation/dirty/apply for global settings stay private to s3; it exposes only sc2 for the override editors.
The per-repo overrides sub-section (models.byRepo.<repoPath>.*) is wholly private to s5; it plugs into sc3's section seam and reuses sc2.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase D — Dynamic-key override editors (per-role, per-repo)

nonFunctional.performance: One config.catalog round-trip + the config.show read on open; rendering the roles is trivial Swing work. No polling; reads on open and after Apply.
nonFunctional.security: No new surface beyond the existing local Unix-socket transport; writes go only to config.json via config.write.
nonFunctional.observability: config.write logs each write; the plugin surfaces daemon-unavailable and write-rejected states rather than failing silently.
nonFunctional.durability: Persistence unchanged — the daemon's config.json write + reconcile own durability; the plugin never writes config.json directly.

api.name: DaemonGateway.perRoleOverrides

returns.meaning: Loaded(overrides: Map<String,String>) = the current models.tasks { roleId -> tierName } read over the EXISTING config.show IPC; Unavailable(reason) when the daemon is unreachable / a transport fault. No new daemon code.

errors.condition: DaemonUnavailableException / a RuntimeException from the config.show call (never throws).

preconditions: None — global read, no params (config.show is global).
postconditions: Parses data.models.tasks into a Map<String,String>; a missing/non-map models or tasks yields a Loaded empty map (distinct from Unavailable).
Only string-valued entries kept (a non-string tier skipped); never a partial throw.

api.name: PerRoleOverridesModel
api.signature: class PerRoleOverridesModel(roles: List<RoleDto>, tierNames: List<String>, current: Map<String,String>) { fun rows(): List<PerRoleRow>; fun setOverride(roleId: String, tier: String): Unit; fun removeOverride(roleId: String): Unit; fun revert(): Unit; fun isModified(): Boolean; fun collectWrites(): List<PendingWrite>; fun onSaved(roleId: String): Unit }

parameters.name: roles
parameters.purpose: The recognized roles (id + defaultTier) from sc1 — daemon-derived (lc1), never hardcoded.

parameters.name: tierNames
parameters.purpose: The allowed tier names from sc1 (cheap/mid/core) — chooser options + validation domain.

parameters.name: current
parameters.purpose: The current models.tasks overrides (roleId -> tier) from the config.show read; present = override, absent = default routing.

returns.meaning: The pure, headless per-role editor state: override-vs-default rows, add/change/remove intent, dirty, and the roleId->segment mapping. Load-bearing logic lives here (not the Swing section) so it is unit-testable.

errors.condition: setOverride/removeOverride with a roleId not in `roles`, or setOverride with a tier not in `tierNames` (programmer error).

preconditions: setOverride's tier is one of tierNames.
postconditions: rows() returns one PerRoleRow per role {roleId, effectiveTier, isOverride}, reflecting PENDING state; effectiveTier = pending override tier when overridden else defaultTier (ac1).
isModified() true iff any role's pending override differs from its `current` state.

collectWrites() returns only changed roles as PendingWrite(listOf("models","tasks",roleId), Set(tier)) for add/change and (..., Clear) for a removal — roleId is ONE literal segment (dots intact), per-key isolation (ac2/ac3).
onSaved(roleId) advances that role's `current` baseline and clears its dirty flag.
Selecting the same tier a role already overrides to is NOT dirty; removing a role with no override is a no-op.

api.name: PerRoleSection
api.signature: class PerRoleSection(model: PerRoleOverridesModel, gateway: DaemonGateway) : SettingsSection { override val title: String; override fun component(): JComponent; override fun isModified(): Boolean; override fun apply(); override fun reset() }

parameters.name: model
parameters.purpose: The pure per-role edit state the section renders + drives.

parameters.name: gateway
parameters.purpose: The sc2 write surface (writeSetting/clearSetting) the section applies through.

returns.meaning: The per-role sub-section plugged into the sc3 seam: a thin Swing shell of role rows (tier chooser + use-default/remove) bound to the model. apply() runs collectWrites via sc2 and advances onSaved on Saved; isModified/reset delegate to the model.

errors.condition: apply surfaces a not-Saved SaveResult to the host so the host throws ConfigurationException preserving the pending intent (returned to the host, not thrown raw).

preconditions: Rendered only on a Loaded catalog; an Unavailable page installs no section.
postconditions: apply writes only changed roles via sc2 with the literal segment array; a Saved role advances the model; a not-Saved role keeps its pending intent and is surfaced (ac2/ac3, never a false success).
Registers NO new shared contract; consumes sc1/sc2/sc3 only.

api.name: InsrcSettingsConfigurable.apply
api.signature: override fun apply(): Unit  // + isModified(), reset(), createComponent host glue for SettingsSection

returns.meaning: The host now also drives registered SettingsSections: createComponent renders each section below the global groups; isModified() ORs the global model with any section.isModified(); apply() runs the global dirty writes AND each section's writes in the SAME off-EDT ProgressManager block, then throws ConfigurationException if any failed; reset() reverts the global model AND each section. Minimal glue activating the sc3 seam s2 declared.

errors.condition: any global field or section write returns not-Saved, or a validation error — thrown after the off-EDT writes so the dialog stays open with edits preserved (ac2/ac3).

preconditions: Loaded catalog; sections built from the same catalog + the perRoleOverrides read.
postconditions: Per-key isolation: each section write is an independent sc2 call at one literal key; a partial failure advances only the Saved ones.
Writes run OFF the EDT (S003 pattern); model/section mutation + re-seed back on the EDT.

dataModelChanges.details: New sealed interface in the daemon package: Loaded(val overrides: Map<String,String>) | Unavailable(val reason: String). The config.show-backed perRoleOverrides() result; two-state (mirrors SettingsCatalogResult) so an unreachable daemon is distinct from a legitimately-empty override map.

New pure row DTO in the settings package: {roleId: String, effectiveTier: String, isOverride: Boolean}. What the section renders per role (ac1). Reuses PendingWrite/WriteOp from S003 for collectWrites().
Per-role pure state: the RoleDto, the current-override tier (or none), the pending intent (override-to-tier / removed / unchanged). Private to s4.

The host gains a list of SettingsSection built on Loaded (S003 rendered only global groups); createComponent renders them and isModified/apply/reset fan out to them — activating the sc3 seam s2 declared but left unused.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Consumes settingsCatalog()'s roles (id+defaultTier) + tierNames UNCHANGED for the rows + chooser (lc1). Does NOT amend sc1: the CURRENT override values come from the existing config.show read (perRoleOverrides), not a grown catalog payload.

Consumes writeSetting/clearSetting VERBATIM: add/change = writeSetting(listOf("models","tasks",roleId), tier); removal = clearSetting(listOf("models","tasks",roleId)). roleId is ONE literal segment (dotted roleId never mis-nested, k4; per-key isolation, ac2/ac3). Reuses the S003 SaveResult + off-EDT apply.

Consumes the SettingsSection seam s2 declared: provides PerRoleSection : SettingsSection + minimal host glue to render registered sections and fan isModified/apply/reset. Activates the declared extension point; does not redesign sc3.

errorCases.scenario: The daemon is unreachable when reading the current per-role overrides on page open.
errorCases.detection: perRoleOverrides() catches DaemonUnavailableException/RuntimeException from config.show and returns PerRoleOverridesResult.Unavailable(reason).
errorCases.response: The section renders an unavailable placeholder and installs no editable rows; consistent with the settingsCatalog Unavailable page.
errorCases.userImpact: The section is shown unavailable rather than an empty/misleading role list; retry on reopen.

errorCases.scenario: A per-role override write is rejected by the daemon (config.write ok=false).
errorCases.detection: sc2.writeSetting/clearSetting returns SaveResult.Rejected (data['ok']==false) — the S003 classification.
errorCases.response: The host apply does not advance that role via onSaved, keeps the pending intent, collects the failure, throws ConfigurationException naming the role; other roles' Saved writes stand.
errorCases.userImpact: Clear failure; the pending override/removal preserved; never a false success (ac2/ac3).

errorCases.scenario: The daemon drops mid-apply after some role writes succeeded.
errorCases.detection: a later write throws DaemonUnavailableException -> SaveResult.Unavailable; the host records it in failures.
errorCases.response: Already-Saved roles advanced; failed + remaining roles keep pending intent; apply throws ConfigurationException summarizing failures.
errorCases.userImpact: Honest partial progress; no override silently lost (ac2/ac3).

errorCases.scenario: config.show returns a config whose models.tasks is present but not a JSON object.
errorCases.detection: perRoleOverrides's `as? Map` cast fails -> treated as no overrides (empty); non-string entries skipped.
errorCases.response: The editor shows every role as default routing rather than throwing; the developer can still add overrides.
errorCases.userImpact: Degrades to 'no overrides' instead of a crash.

edgeCases.input: A roleId that contains dots (e.g. 'design.contract.detail') is overridden.
edgeCases.expected: collectWrites emits PendingWrite(listOf("models","tasks","design.contract.detail"), Set(tier)) — roleId ONE segment; config.write keys models.tasks['design.contract.detail'] flat (k4/ac2).

edgeCases.input: Set a role's override to the SAME tier it already overrides to.
edgeCases.expected: Not dirty; collectWrites omits it; no write.

edgeCases.input: Set a role's override equal to its defaultTier.
edgeCases.expected: An explicit override write (models.tasks.<roleId> = defaultTier) — dirty vs 'no override', written, NOT auto-converted to a removal; removal is the separate use-default affordance.

edgeCases.input: Mark a removal on a role that has an override, then revert before apply.
edgeCases.expected: revert() restores every role to `current`; isModified()=false; no daemon call.

edgeCases.input: The daemon has an override for a roleId NOT in the recognized role set.
edgeCases.expected: rows() lists only recognized roles (lc1); the unknown key is not shown and is left untouched (per-key isolation).

edgeCases.input: The per-role overrides map is empty.
edgeCases.expected: Every recognized role listed as default routing (ac1); isModified()=false until a change.

invariantsToPreserve.text: The overridable roles + tier names come from the daemon's recognized taxonomy (sc1), never hardcoded (lc1).

A per-role write goes through config.write with a LITERAL [models, tasks, roleId] segment array so a dotted roleId is never mis-nested; per-key isolation — one role's key never disturbs another or the surrounding models.tasks map.

The plugin talks to the daemon only over the existing Unix-socket transport and honours its framing (config.show returns the object directly; config.write's ok lives in data); no new transport, no direct config.json write.
The daemon stays the single source of truth: removing an override CLEARS the key so the role falls back to the daemon's default routing.

dirty semantics: same-tier not dirty; remove-of-unset no-op; default-tier is an explicit override
collectWrites: Set at listOf('models','tasks',roleId) / Clear; a DOTTED roleId stays ONE segment (ac2/ac3, k4)
per-key isolation: one changed role -> exactly one PendingWrite

testStrategy.testFramework: JUnit5 (org.junit.jupiter) on JDK21 via ./gradlew test, matching S002/S003's SettingsEditModelTest/SettingsWriteGatewayTest; source-scan tests read the Kotlin source. No BasePlatformTestCase and no daemon/TS test (config.show + config.write reused unchanged).

migration.stateBefore: After S003 (main c5eab8f) the page edits the GLOBAL catalog settings via sc2 with a pure SettingsEditModel + off-EDT apply. The sc3 SettingsSection interface is declared but the InsrcSettingsConfigurable host NEVER renders a section. The gateway has no read of the dynamic per-role overrides (models.tasks.<roleId>); sc1's `values` carries only the ~31 static paths. config.show + config.write exist and are unchanged.
migration.stateAfter: The page shows a per-role overrides sub-section below the global groups: each recognized role with its effective tier + override-vs-default, add/change (writeSetting models.tasks.<roleId>=tier) and remove (clearSetting) via sc2. A thin perRoleOverrides read over config.show supplies the current overrides; a pure PerRoleOverridesModel owns the logic; PerRoleSection plugs into the now-activated sc3 host glue. Daemon UNCHANGED; s5 not built.

migrationSteps.action: Add PerRoleOverridesResult + DaemonGateway.perRoleOverrides() over config.show + the DaemonGatewayService delegate + stubs in the 4 test doubles. Additive to the interface.
Add the pure PerRoleOverridesModel + PerRoleRow (+ RoleState) reusing PendingWrite/WriteOp; no existing-symbol changes.
Add PerRoleSection : SettingsSection + the minimal host glue in InsrcSettingsConfigurable (section list on Loaded, render below groups, fan isModified/apply(off-EDT)/reset). Activates the sc3 seam.
Extend the test suite (PerRoleOverridesModelTest, perRoleOverrides gateway Fake+WireRpc, Configurable source-scan) and run ./gradlew test on JDK21.

migration.backwardCompat: The DaemonGateway interface only GAINS perRoleOverrides() (+ 4 test-double stubs); settingsCatalog/writeSetting/clearSetting and all S001-S003 behaviour unchanged. config.show + config.write reused verbatim — no daemon code change, config.json stays valid, older/newer daemons interoperate. A per-role write lands at models.tasks.<roleId> (the daemon's existing dynamic-key namespace); per-key isolation leaves existing overrides untouched. A page against an Unavailable daemon renders no section. No migration or data rewrite.

alternativesConsidered.name: config.show read + generic SettingsSection registry + pure per-role model
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A thin gateway read over the existing config.show yields the current models.tasks map; a pure PerRoleOverridesModel owns the logic; a PerRoleSection : SettingsSection plugs into the host, which renders registered sections generically and fans apply/isModified/reset to them.
alternativesConsidered.approach: perRoleOverrides() over config.show -> Map<roleId,tier>; PerRoleOverridesModel(roles, tierNames, current) exposes rows/setOverride/removeOverride/revert/isModified/collectWrites/onSaved with roleId as one literal segment; PerRoleSection : SettingsSection; minimal host glue renders sections + fans apply/isModified/reset; s5 reuses the same glue.
pros: Reads current overrides from an EXISTING daemon IPC (config.show) named in the HLD — no daemon change, no sc1 amendment.
Load-bearing logic (override-vs-default, dotted roleId->segments, add/change/remove, dirty) is pure + headless-testable.
Activates the sc3 seam generically so s5 reuses it with zero further host change.
Reuses sc2 verbatim + the S003 off-EDT apply.
cons: A second read round-trip (config.catalog + config.show) on open — trivial for a local socket.
The host-glue edit touches s2's file (mitigated: only consumes the declared seam).
A new gateway read even though s4 owns no contract — an s4-internal consumption, not a shared contract.

alternativesConsidered.name: Amend sc1 to include current per-role override values in the catalog payload
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Propose an HLD amendment (sharedContract.fieldAdd) so config.catalog also carries the current models.tasks overrides, read from the existing settingsCatalog().
alternativesConsidered.approach: fieldAdd roleOverrides to SettingsCatalogPayload/DTO; the daemon's buildSettingsCatalog folds config's models.tasks in; the section reads catalog.roleOverrides. Same pure model + host glue otherwise.
pros: One read instead of two; overrides arrive with the roles/tierNames.
cons: Requires editing s1's daemon code + the sc1 DTO — inside s1's adjacent boundary, needs an HLD amendment + re-approval for a value config.show already provides.
Couples s4's rollout to an sc1 change.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Only partial on sc1: it redesigns another story's contract + daemon code for a capability the existing config.show already exposes; a1 gets the same result within s4's boundary.

alternativesConsidered.name: config.show read but hardcode the per-role section in the Configurable (logic in the shell)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Same config.show read, but build the per-role rows + add/change/remove logic directly inside InsrcSettingsConfigurable instead of a pure model + generic SettingsSection.
alternativesConsidered.approach: perRoleOverrides() read as in a1, but the Configurable constructs the rows inline, tracks dirty by walking combo boxes, and calls sc2 in apply — no pure model, no generic section list.
cons: Load-bearing override/dirty/dotted-segment logic lives in the untestable Swing shell — the silent-defect gap (ac1/ac2/ac3 effectively untested).
Leaves the sc3 seam dead and forces s5 to duplicate inline host code.
Walking live combo boxes for dirty state is fragile + EDT-coupled; the dotted-key mapping is buried.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Partial on ac1/ac2/ac3 (logic in the untestable shell) and partial on sc3 (seam unused) — the exact pattern the review split exists to prevent.

citations.quotedText: buildSettingsCatalog: roles = taxonomy.roles.map({id, defaultTier}); tierNames = Object.keys(taxonomy.rankOf) (cheap/mid/core) — the daemon-derived role set/tiers sc1 delivers.
buildSettingsCatalog `values` is populated only for the static CONFIG_CATALOG paths; the dynamic models.tasks.<roleId> keys never appear in it.
interface SettingsSection { title; component(); isModified(); apply(); reset() } declared as the sc3 seam but never rendered by the host (renderBody builds only the catalog groups).
config.show returns the raw config object directly (parse-or-{}), so data.models.tasks is the current { roleId: tier } map; the transport framing is the existing Unix-socket JSON-RPC.
models.tasks.<roleId> keys contain dots; sc2 writeSetting/clearSetting take a LITERAL List<String> so roleId is one segment; setConfigAtPath sets/removes only that leaf (per-key isolation).

citations.ref: HLD constraint k5 / CLAUDE.md project principles
citations.quotedText: Changing which values are stored is the daemon's job; the plugin owns no settings semantics or defaults — removing an override clears the key so the daemon default governs.
